title: Two of Home's own choices become decision points: how a question is computed, and a column kept out on statistics alone
request: The owner chose 'Students, data first': before more student models, the choices Home makes and no point recorded should be captured with their labels.
spec: query.plan (workflow, on the draft): the plan's shape (operation and column, grouping columns, grain, filtered columns; names only), the rules' or a model's, labelled by the plan of the first answer the person keeps for the question. column.statistics_only (technical, on the column): the rule's recommendation (feature or keep_out) against the person's answer in the column check, with the column's bands and what the rule read.
plan: Add the two points and three state fields in dclab_core's ledger; record them in dclab_rnd's capture where Home makes the choice.
Keep every value out of the state and the answers: a plan's shape holds column names, never a filter's value.
Label each with what the person did, and say which labels count.
List both in the main product's conformance and the workflow models' NOT_LEARNED with the reason.

decisions.decision: Only a save labels query.plan; an edit alone labels nothing.
decisions.why: The edit controls change the operation, the split or the grain, which is often a person looking at another view rather than correcting a wrong plan; keeping one answer is what they chose.

decisions.decision: A kept answer nobody changed is recorded as agreement, which never counts.
decisions.why: A person shown the answer who agrees is not evidence that it was right (effective_label); the record says so instead of claiming a positive label.

decisions.decision: column.statistics_only is about the column, with its bands from the draft's profile.
decisions.why: On the draft, two disputed columns gave records nobody could tell apart or join to the same column's feature.leakage_suspect record, and a student could only copy the rule.

change: dclab_core/ledger.py: points query.plan and column.statistics_only, state fields brief_fields, reviewer, names_moment (dclab-core 0.134.0, CHANGELOG); adapters/conformance.py POINTS_NOT_MAPPED and workflow_labels.NOT_LEARNED entries; dclab_rnd/ledger/capture.py plan_shape, query_planned (planner, rules_asked), query_judged, column_checked (REVIEWER_CODES, the column's bands); draft/chat.py give_answer records the plan with its planner, save_answer labels the question's first plan once inside the store update, column_answer passes the profile; the query_data tool passes planner home_agent. Tests in test_home_answer and test_home_column_check; data catalog regenerated.

findings.defect: A column the leakage reviewer read as late was never recorded.
findings.scenario: The reviewer said 'after the moment', the usual case where the rule says keep_out: the record was refused and silently lost.
findings.cause: The verdict went into the state as a code, and 'after the moment' is not a lower-case key.
findings.fix: The verdicts are mapped to codes (available, after_moment, else none).

findings.defect: Two gate tests failed on the new points.
findings.scenario: test_conformance and test_workflow_models: every point is mapped to the main product or says why not, and every workflow point is learned or says why not.
findings.cause: Neither list had the new points.
findings.fix: Both points in POINTS_NOT_MAPPED and query.plan in NOT_LEARNED, each with its reason.

findings.defect: column.statistics_only did not say which column it was about.
findings.scenario: Two disputed columns in one draft gave records with the same subject and state, joined to neither column's leakage record.
findings.cause: The subject was the draft and the state held only what the rule read.
findings.fix: The subject is the column, with the draft id beside it, and the state holds the column's bands from the draft's profile.

findings.defect: The Home agent's own plans were credited to the wrong answerers.
findings.scenario: The query_data tool answered a question: the record showed the rules abstaining, though they were never asked, and the plan credited to home_query rather than home_agent.
findings.cause: give_answer knew only that a model planned, not which one or whether the rules were asked.
findings.fix: give_answer takes the planner; the rules' answer is written only on the path that asked them.

findings.defect: The 'kept' half of query.plan's labels could never count, and every edit labelled the first plan.
findings.scenario: A person kept an answer unchanged: the agreeing label never counted. A person who switched to another view labelled the first plan wrong.
findings.cause: A label from a person shown the answer counts only when it disagrees; edits were read as corrections.
findings.fix: Only the first save labels, with the kept answer's plan; an edit alone labels nothing; agreement is documented as never counting.

findings.defect: Two saves at once could write the label twice.
findings.scenario: A double click on Keep runs two saves on two threads.
findings.cause: The judged check and its setting were outside the store update.
findings.fix: judged is set inside the update and only the call that set it writes the label.

outcome: Home's way of computing a question and its column check are recorded on the right subject, credited to the answerer that gave them, with labels that say what the person chose.
lessons: Before writing a label, ask whether the ledger will ever count it: a label that can only agree with what the person was shown is a record of agreement, not of being right.
risks: A question whose answers are never kept stays unlabelled, so query.plan's labels will come mostly from people who corrected a plan.
